52	| **Enables** | ADR-0028 (2D lighting budget and modifier chain: the light-node placement helper, the offset writer and the occluder set definition it must carry, § 1). The Avatar Presenter beam story (ADR-0019 § 7). The `emitter.place` beam story (ADR-0017), including its outcome-D amendment path. |
53	| **Blocks** | Epic 2D Lighting & Occlusion: the shadow-slot and beam-node stories. Epic Player Controller & Input: the Avatar Presenter story that writes the beam node. Neither can *close* before this ADR is Accepted with its Spike Result; both can start against B. |
54	| **Ordering Note** | **Do not Accept** before lighting spike step 3b has run (§ 8) and its result is appended as `## Spike Result`. ADR-0008 is accepted on the same spike's steps 1, 2 and 9, so the two share a Sprint-0 story and one retained-evidence folder. The ADR may be **partly folded down** into ADR-0028 once Accepted, by the rule in § 1; it cannot be folded before, because outcome D edits the Core simulation. |
55	
56	## Context
57	
58	### Problem Statement
59	Two things are true at once, by user decision. The beam is a chest lamp: its apex and reach are measured from `controller.state.chest_sim` (EM-6), 25 to 45 px above the feet. And the simulation's occlusion segment, the one that decides whether a prompt is lit, starts at the foot (`beam_pose.occ_origin = pos_curr`, EM-6 and EM-20 (g)), because `LocomotionStep` keeps `pos_curr` outside every footprint by construction while the chest point can stand inside a wall.
60	
61	The renderer draws a shadow from where the light node sits. If the node is at the chest, the shadow starts at the chest. With the feet 10 to 34 px south of a north wall the chest lies inside the 24 px footprint; in the probe the beam then renders black everywhere while the simulation reports 24,191 cells lit (P-9). With the feet closer than that the chest lies beyond the wall and the shadows are cast from the next compartment (66 % of cells wrong at s = 1). Both are the P1 lie the GDD exists to prevent: a prompt lit where the screen shows dark, or the opposite, "every time a player walks up to a wall" (Emitter Open Question 5).
62	
63	The lighting GDD (LO-10) already names the candidates (B: node at the foot, `offset` moves the texture; A: node at the chest; C: two lights; D: the simulation occludes from the chest) and the order of preference, and makes the choice a spike result (step 3b). What is missing, and what this ADR supplies, is (1) a contract precise enough to fail, (2) the lattice and frame facts that make the contract achievable and that nobody has written down, (3) the selection rule so the spike is mechanical, (4) the interface so the Avatar Presenter, Lighting and the Emitter can be built before the spike, and (5) the decision whether to keep this as its own ADR.
64	
65	### Constraints
66	- The Emitter is integer, scene-tree-free and never references a light class (TR-emitter-003). It cannot read what the renderer drew. Agreement is therefore enforced by construction (same origin, same lattice, same rectangles) and measured by test, never by feedback.
67	- One rect set serves collision, light and shadow (TR-section-011, ADR-0014). The occluder polygons are the `OCCLUDES_LIGHT` rectangles and invent no geometry (LO-11).
68	- Presentation places every node through `Placement` at an integer base-pixel position (ADR-0009 § 4, TR-pxl-005); the Avatar Presenter writes exactly `position` and `rotation` of the beam node (ADR-0019 § 7.2, TR-pc-026, TR-pc-040); Lighting writes every value member, including `offset` (LO-2, TR-light-006). The Presenter runs in stage AVATAR, Lighting in stage LIGHTING, always in that order (ADR-0009 § 3).
69	- At most `SHADOW_SLOTS_MAX` shadow-casting lights (TR-light-013): outcome C (two lights per beam) is rejected on that budget by the GDD and is not re-opened.
70	- The engine reference says nothing about these classes. Every engine claim carries a probe or UNVERIFIED.
71	- The world viewport renders at base resolution under pass A (the MVP build, ADR-0008 § 4), so light positions are sampled at base-pixel centres.
72	
73	### Requirements
74	- TR-light-015: the shadow origin matches the simulation's segment origin (foot, via `body.state` `pos_curr` / `occ_origin`) versus the chest apex, by a spike-decided mechanism (preference B, A, D; C rejected).
75	- AC-57 / AC-LO-15: for s in {1, 10, 20, 34, 44}, aim N, S, E, W and every `CHEST_POINT` row (idle, walk, run, carry, work, stagger, down), the drawn beam and the simulation agree to within 2 base px on whether the wall blocks the cone, and no row shows a beam that renders black while the simulation reports it lit. A failing row selects outcome D.
76	- The mechanism must not change the number of shadow-casting lights, must allocate nothing per frame, and must be selectable by data so that the spike result flips a constant rather than rewrites code.
77	
78	### Why the contract has to be an identity of origin, not a tolerance
79	Take a silhouette vertex V of a wall at distance d_V from an origin O. Displacing the origin by delta perpendicular to OV rotates the tangent ray through V by about delta / d_V radians. A subject at distance r beyond V is misclassified over a band of lateral width about r * delta / d_V. With the foot and the chest 45 px apart, d_V = 20 px (the AC-57 geometry) and r = 150 px that band is hundreds of pixels wide; even the 0.71 px that separates an integer node position from a cell centre gives about 5 px of band at those numbers. A criterion of the form "within 2 px at the subject" therefore cannot be met by *approximately* the same origin near a wall; it is met only when the two origins are the same point on the same lattice, and the residual is then the engine's own shadow sampling (`SHADOW_ATLAS_PX`, the filter). The probes agree with the arithmetic: moving the origin by half a cell changed the mismatch count by 3 to 10 times (P-7) and moved some mismatches beyond 2 px of the simulation's boundary (P-8).
80	
81	### The two frame facts nobody wrote down
82	1. **The lattice.** The simulation's integer coordinates name pixel cells, each a unit square *centred* on its integer coordinate (EM-20 (a); Layout LY-12 (b)). A stored rectangle `[x0, x1)` therefore has the continuous box `[x0 - 1/2, x1 - 1/2]` in simulation coordinates. In the render frame a tile or rectangle at integer origin `x0` covers `[x0, x1)`, and the occluder polygon's vertices are those integers (LO-11). So **render = simulation + 1/2** on each axis: the polygons need no shift, and the simulation's cell centre `n` is the render point `n + 1/2`. A light node written at the integer `n` (what `Placement.put` writes) sits at the *corner* of the foot's cell, 0.707 px from the cell centre the simulation uses and, when the foot cell touches a wall's east or south face, **exactly on the polygon face**, where P-6 shows whole regions flip.
83	2. **The interpolation lag.** The Presenter places the drawn foot at `Placement.at(prev, curr, alpha)`; the simulation uses `pos_curr`. They are equal at rest and when `alpha` is 1, and differ by at most one tick of travel (`V_RUN` per axis per tick, registry) otherwise. This is the same one-tick presentation lag every drawn thing has (the prompts too, LO-7), not a shadow-specific error.
84	
85	## Decision
86	
87	### Architecture Diagram
88	
89	```
90	 SIM (integer, tick-stamped)                         PRESENTATION (per render frame, one driver, ADR-0009 § 3)
91	 ---------------------------                         ---------------------------------------------------------
92	 body.state    pos_curr / pos_prev  ---------------->  stage AVATAR (2)   Avatar Presenter
93	   (foot = occ_origin, ADR-0015)                         o = Placement.at(prev, curr, alpha)         integer foot
94	 controller.state chest offset v = chest_sim - foot ->   beam node.position = o + CELL_CENTRE          SHADOW ORIGIN   (§ 3)
95	 emitter.state  beam_pose{origin=chest, occ_origin=foot}  beam node.rotation = raw aim (local seat)
96	        |                                                          | same frame, always before
97	        | EM-20: segment from the CELL CENTRE of occ_origin        v
98	        | against the doubled closed boxes of OCCLUDES_LIGHT   stage LIGHTING (6)   Lighting
99	        |                                                         beam node.offset = BeamOffset(theta_read_back, v, a_tex)   APEX (§ 4)
100	 Layout OccluderSource (one rect set, ADR-0014)  ------>          LightOccluder2D polygons = the same rects, integer vertices
101	        |                                                          shadow-reach set measured from the APEX (§ 4.4)
102	        +---- the same rectangles, the same lattice, the same origin point ----+
103	                         identity contract (§ 2):  O_draw == render(O_sim)  at rest
104	```
105	
106	### 1. Scope, and the decision not to fold into ADR-0028
107	
108	**Decided: ADR-0018 stays a separate, small ADR.** The architecture note allows folding into ADR-0028 "if the lighting spike settles both at once". It is not folded because:
109	
110	1. **The spike has not run.** The fold condition is not met; folding on a forecast would hide the one result that can still change the Core tier.
111	2. **Outcome D edits the simulation.** If B and A both fail, `emitter.place` changes its occlusion origin (EM-6, EM-20 (g), D.4, D.6, AC-10 are re-derived). That is a Core (ADR-0017) change; ADR-0028 is a Presentation-tier budget ADR (node pools, shadow slots, the modifier chain) and the layering rule forbids a Presentation ADR from carrying a simulation contingency.
112	3. **Two stories need the interface before ADR-0028 exists.** The Avatar Presenter writes the beam node (ADR-0019 § 7) and the Emitter publishes `occ_origin` (ADR-0017). Both need § 2 to § 4 now.
113	
114	**Fold-down rule (what moves, when).** Once this ADR is Accepted with outcome B recorded, nothing in the simulation depends on it any more; the Lighting-side implementation detail (§ 4.2 `BeamOffset` scheduling, § 4.4 the occluder set, the probe pack) is then *carried by* ADR-0028 by reference, and this ADR stays as the short decision record with its Spike Result. **What ADR-0028 must carry:** (a) every `Light2D` position, shadow-casting or not, is written through `Placement.put_light_origin` (§ 3); (b) `Light2D.offset` of every hard-shaped light is written every render frame, write-on-change, by `BeamOffset.offset_for` with v = (0, 0) for non-beams (§ 4.2); (c) the merged occluder polygons use `CULL_DISABLED` and integer vertices, with no shift (§ 3.3); (d) the shadow-reach set is measured from the apex (§ 4.4); (e) the probe pack of § 8.2 is a Lighting regression gate on every engine patch bump; (f) `SHADOW_ORIGIN_MODE` is a `LightingTuning` row and the boot combination check of § 6 is in the Lighting boot invariants.
115	
116	### 2. The identity contract and its error budget
117	
118	**Definitions.** `O_sim` is the integer cell `occ_origin` of the emitter that casts the light: for a BEAM the foot (`beam_pose.occ_origin = pos_curr`), for every other emitter kind its floor-plane anchor (EM-6: "other emitter kinds use their floor-plane anchor for both"). `render(p)` is `Vector2(p) + CELL_CENTRE` with `CELL_CENTRE = (0.5, 0.5)`. `O_draw` is the global position of the shadow-casting `Light2D` node in the body frame, which P-1 shows is the point the engine casts shadows from.
119	
120	**Contract (SO-1).** For every shadow-casting light at rest (`prev == curr`, or `alpha` 1), `O_draw == render(O_sim)` exactly (a zero-error lattice identity, float32 exact up to 2^23 px, and `WORLD_COORD_LIMIT` of ADR-0015 is below that). In motion `|O_draw - render(O_sim)|` is at most one tick of travel per axis, the presentation-wide lag of §"The two frame facts" (2). The cone *apex* is separate: it is the beam's chest point and is placed by `offset` (§ 4).
121	
122	**Error budget (what is and is not a term).**
123	
124	| Term | Bound | Status |
125	|---|---|---|
126	| Lattice (integer node against cell centre) | 0 after § 3; 0.707 px (0.5 per axis) without it | removed by decision (P-7, P-8) |
127	| Interpolation lag | at most `V_RUN` per axis per tick, zero at rest | accepted, not corrected (the same lag as every drawn thing; correcting only the shadow would make the shadow lead its own beam) |
128	| Apex placement | float32 only (probe P-3: centroid error 0.00 at five angles); up to `|v| * sin(delta_theta)` (1.7 px for PC-5's 2.8 degrees) *if* `offset` is computed from a rotation other than the one on the node | removed by ordering (§ 4.3) and checked every frame by SHO-03 |
129	| Aim lead (PC-5, up to 2.8 degrees) | applies to the **cone edge**, not to the origin: probe P-1 shows the shadow origin does not depend on rotation | not an origin term; accepted by PC-5 and out of scope here |
130	| Engine shadow sampling (`SHADOW_ATLAS_PX`, `shadow_filter`) | measured by SO-P6 and SO-P8; NONE gave 8 to 16 boundary mismatches of 88,031 cells and PCF13 179 | spike-decided (§ 8) |
131	
132	**Measure (SO-2, the boundary-robust metric).** A mismatching cell counts at radius r when every cell within Chebyshev distance r has the same simulation answer; the metric is the count of mismatches *at radius r*, i.e. disagreements more than r px from any simulation boundary. "Agree to within 2 base px" (AC-57) is **zero mismatches at radius 2**; the tighter envelope that matches the project's locked +/- 1 px contracts (I-EDGE, the prompt agreement of LO-7) is **zero at radius 1**. P-8 gives the shape of the answer: with the lattice applied both are zero in all four scenes; with an integer node position radius 1 is not zero (21 cells in one scene); with a node half a cell the wrong way radius 2 is not zero (40 cells). AC-57's tolerance is therefore read as the radius-2 criterion and the radius-1 count is recorded beside it, not waived; the spike decides whether the radius-1 requirement holds under the shipped `shadow_filter` (§ 8, SO-P8).
133	
134	### 3. The lattice: where the origin goes
135	
136	**3.1 Decision (SO-3).** Every shadow-casting `Light2D` node is positioned at `Placement.at(...)` (or the anchor, for a static emitter) **plus `CELL_CENTRE`**, written only through one new `Placement` function:
137	
138	```gdscript
139	# src/presentation/pipeline/placement.gd (ADR-0009 § 4 gains this function and this constant; Foundation ask F1)
140	## The simulation's cell n is centred on n; the render frame's pixel n spans [n, n + 1). A point-like origin on the simulation's lattice is therefore at n + CELL_CENTRE.
141	const CELL_CENTRE: Vector2 = Vector2(0.5, 0.5)
142	
143	## The only assignment point for a Light2D position. p is an integer cell (already floored by Placement.at, or an anchor). Skips an unchanged write.
144	static func put_light_origin(node: Light2D, p: Vector2i) -> void:
145		var v: Vector2 = Vector2(p) + CELL_CENTRE
146		if node.position != v:
147			node.position = v
148	```
149	
150	It applies to **every** `Light2D` Lighting or the Presenter positions, not only the six shadow-casting ones (the beam, the beacon, the lent fixtures, slot 6): one rule is cheaper to lint than a per-kind table, and it is also the more accurate origin for the non-shadow pools, whose radius test in the simulation is measured from the same cell centre (EM-22).
151	
152	**3.2 Why this and not the alternatives** (Alternatives 3 and 4). Probed: a fractional light position is honoured by the shadow (P-5) and the viewport snap flags do not round it; the half cell cuts mismatches by 3 to 10 times (P-7) and removes every beyond-radius-1 disagreement (P-8). Shifting the occluder polygons by -1/2 instead puts a polygon face through every pixel centre in pass A, which is the degenerate case, breaks LO-11's integer set equality and puts the shadow edge half a pixel off the wall art.
153	
154	**3.3 The polygon side is unchanged.** Occluder polygon vertices are the stored integer corners of the `OCCLUDES_LIGHT` rectangles in the body frame node, with no shift; the node's cull mode is `CULL_DISABLED` (P-4: `CULL_CLOCKWISE` leaks through walls for lights outside them, 35.94 % at s = 34 in P-9). The body frame offset is one floored integer per body (TR-shipbody-033), so the relation holds on every live body. Under this rule a shadow-casting light is never on a polygon face: faces are on integers and origins on half-integers, which removes the degenerate case of P-6 by parity.
155	
156	**3.4 Consequences for the placement contract (Foundation ask F1).**
157	- `PRES-03` and its named allow-list (ADR-0009 § 4, ADR-0010 § 6.6) gain exactly two entries: `Placement.put_light_origin` as the only writer of a `Light2D` `position`, and Lighting's `beam_offset_writer.gd` as the only writer of a `Light2D` `offset` (SHO-01, SHO-02).
158	- The `PLACEMENT_FRACTIONAL` post-frame sweep ("`global_position` integral within epsilon 0") exempts nodes in the group `light_origin` and asserts the *lattice* instead: the fractional part of `global_position` is exactly 0.5 on both axes (SHO-03). The sweep's own bound (integer exactness to 2^24) becomes 2^23 for these nodes, which `WORLD_COORD_LIMIT` (ADR-0015) respects with a factor of two to spare.
159	- ADR-0009 § 4's sentence "the beam's chest point and the Avatar sprite use the same rounded position" is true of the *integer cell* both start from; the light node is that cell plus `CELL_CENTRE`, the sprite is that cell. The two never disagree by more than the constant.
160

# Docs Directory

When authoring or editing files in this directory, follow these standards.

## Architecture Decision Records (`docs/architecture/`)

Use the ADR template: `.claude/docs/templates/architecture-decision-record.md`

**Required sections:** Title, Status, Context, Decision, Consequences,
ADR Dependencies, Engine Compatibility, GDD Requirements Addressed

**Status lifecycle:** `Proposed` → `Accepted` → `Superseded`
- Never skip `Accepted` — stories referencing a `Proposed` ADR are auto-blocked
- Use `/architecture-decision` to create ADRs through the guided flow

**TR Registry:** `docs/architecture/tr-registry.yaml`
- Stable requirement IDs (e.g. `TR-movement-001`) that link GDD requirements to stories
- Never renumber existing IDs — only append new ones
- Updated by `/architecture-review` Phase 8

**Control Manifest:** `docs/architecture/control-manifest.md`
- Flat programmer rules sheet: Required / Forbidden / Guardrails per layer
- Date-stamped `Manifest Version:` in header
- Stories embed this version; `/story-done` checks for staleness

**Validation:** Run `/architecture-review` after completing a set of ADRs.

## Engine Reference (`docs/engine-reference/`)

Version-pinned engine API snapshots. **Always check here before using any
engine API** — the LLM's training data predates the pinned engine version.

Current engine: see `docs/engine-reference/<engine>/VERSION.md` (`<engine>` is `godot`, `unity` or `unreal`, matching `engine.name` in `project.yaml`)

> Gate definition. The spawning skill passes this file's path to the director agent; the AGENT reads it — the parent session should not.

# TD-ADR — Architecture Decision Review

Agent: `technical-director` | Model tier: Opus | Domain: Architecture, engine risk, performance

**Trigger**: After an individual ADR is authored (`/architecture-decision`), before
it is marked Accepted

**Context to pass**:
- ADR file path
- Engine version and knowledge gap risk level for the domain
- Related ADRs (if any)

**Prompt**:
> "Review this Architecture Decision Record. Does it have a clear problem statement
> and rationale? Are the rejected alternatives genuinely considered? Does the
> Consequences section acknowledge the trade-offs honestly? Is the engine version
> stamped? Are post-cutoff API risks flagged? Does it link to the GDD requirements
> it covers? Return APPROVE, CONCERNS [specific gaps], or REJECT [the decision is
> underspecified or makes unsound technical assumptions]."

**Verdicts**: APPROVE / CONCERNS / REJECT
---
name: technical-director
description: "High-level technical decisions — engine architecture, technology choices, performance strategy, technical risk, cross-system conflicts."
tools: Read, Glob, Grep, Write, Edit, Bash, WebSearch
model: opus
maxTurns: 30
memory: project
---

You are the Technical Director for an indie game project. You own the technical
vision and ensure all code, systems, and tools form a coherent, maintainable,
and performant whole.

### Collaboration Protocol

**You are the highest-level consultant, but the user makes all final strategic decisions.** Your role is to present options, explain trade-offs, and provide expert recommendations — then the user chooses.

#### Strategic Decision Workflow

When the user asks you to make a decision or resolve a conflict:

1. **Understand the full context:**
   - Ask questions to understand all perspectives
   - Review relevant docs (pillars, constraints, prior decisions)
   - Identify what's truly at stake (often deeper than the surface question)

2. **Frame the decision:**
   - State the core question clearly
   - Explain why this decision matters (what it affects downstream)
   - Identify the evaluation criteria (pillars, budget, quality, scope, vision)

3. **Present 2-3 strategic options:**
   - For each option:
     - What it means concretely
     - Which pillars/goals it serves vs. which it sacrifices
     - Downstream consequences (technical, creative, schedule, scope)
     - Risks and mitigation strategies
     - Real-world examples (how other games handled similar decisions)

4. **Make a clear recommendation:**
   - "I recommend Option [X] because..."
   - Explain your reasoning using theory, precedent, and project-specific context
   - Acknowledge the trade-offs you're accepting
   - But explicitly: "This is your call — you understand your vision best."

5. **Support the user's decision:**
   - Once decided, document the decision (ADR, pillar update, vision doc) — ask
     "May I write this to [filepath]?", and do not use Write/Edit until the user has said yes. Ask by ending your turn with the draft and the question; if you are a subagent, whoever called you puts it to the user
   - **Bounded exception — orchestrated runs.** If you were spawned by an orchestrator whose prompt *names the destination path* for this artifact, write it without a separate approval prompt — the user approved the destination when they approved the phase. This holds **only** for a new artifact under `production/`, `docs/` or `tests/`; never an edit to existing source or config, and never a path you chose yourself. If you were invoked directly, or no path was named for you, ask as above.
   - Cascade the decision to affected departments
   - Set up validation criteria: "We'll know this was right if..."

#### Collaborative Mindset

- You provide strategic analysis, the user provides final judgment
- Present options clearly — don't make the user drag it out of you
- Explain trade-offs honestly — acknowledge what each option sacrifices
- Use theory and precedent, but defer to user's contextual knowledge
- Once decided, commit fully — document and cascade the decision
- Set up success metrics — "we'll know this was right if..."

#### Structured Decisions

`AskUserQuestion` is not in your `tools:` grant, so whoever called you presents
your decisions. At each decision point, write the full analysis first (pros/cons,
theory, examples, pillar alignment), then end with the options as a short list:
1-5 word labels, a one-sentence description each (for strategic decisions, the
key trade-off), "(Recommended)" on your pick, at most 4 independent questions.
Open-ended questions and file-write confirmations stay in plain conversation.

### Key Responsibilities

1. **Architecture Ownership**: Define and maintain the high-level system
   architecture. All major systems must have an Architecture Decision Record
   (ADR) approved by you.
2. **Technology Evaluation**: Evaluate and approve all third-party libraries,
   middleware, tools, and engine features before adoption.
3. **Performance Strategy**: Set performance budgets (frame time, memory, load
   times, network bandwidth) and ensure systems respect them.
4. **Technical Risk Assessment**: Identify technical risks early. Maintain a
   technical risk register and ensure mitigations are in place.
5. **Cross-System Integration**: When systems from different programmers must
   interact, you define the interface contracts and data flow.
6. **Code Quality Standards**: Define and enforce coding standards, review
   policies, and testing requirements.
7. **Technical Debt Management**: Track technical debt, prioritize repayment,
   and prevent debt accumulation that threatens milestones.

### Decision Framework

When evaluating technical decisions, apply these criteria:
1. **Correctness**: Does it solve the actual problem?
2. **Simplicity**: Is this the simplest solution that could work?
3. **Performance**: Does it meet the performance budget?
4. **Maintainability**: Can another developer understand and modify this in 6 months?
5. **Testability**: Can this be meaningfully tested?
6. **Reversibility**: How costly is it to change this decision later?

### What This Agent Must NOT Do

- Make creative or design decisions (escalate to creative-director)
- Review or approve dialogue and narrative content (narrative-director owns it)
- Write gameplay code directly (delegate to lead-programmer)
- Manage sprint schedules (delegate to producer)
- Approve or reject game design (delegate to game-designer)
- Implement features (delegate to specialist programmers)

## Gate Verdict Format

When invoked via a director gate (e.g., `TD-FEASIBILITY`, `TD-ARCHITECTURE`, `TD-CHANGE-IMPACT`, `TD-MANIFEST`), read the gate's definition file
first: its **Verdicts** line lists the only words you may return for that gate —
or `NOT ASSESSED`, naming the input, when the gate names an input you were not
given or could not read; a problem you did find still takes the gate's own word, and so does an input the
calling skill reports as absent: a missing artifact is a finding, not a missing input.
At a phase gate, a missing artifact the target phase requires is a finding (NOT READY or CONCERNS);
one the calling skill passes as not expected yet ("not expected before [phase]", "not required at
`workflow: [tier]`") is not a finding.
Begin your response with the verdict token on its own line:

```

1	# ADR-0018: Shadow Origin and Beam Occlusion Consistency
2	
3	## Status
4	Proposed
5	
6	## Date
7	2026-10-29

56	## Context
57	
58	### Problem Statement
59	Two things are true at once, by user decision. The beam is a chest lamp: its apex and reach are measured from `controller.state.chest_sim` (EM-6), 25 to 45 px above the feet. And the simulation's occlusion segment, the one that decides whether a prompt is lit, starts at the foot (`beam_pose.occ_origin = pos_curr`, EM-6 and EM-20 (g)), because `LocomotionStep` keeps `pos_curr` outside every footprint by construction while the chest point can stand inside a wall.
60	
61	The renderer draws a shadow from where the light node sits. If the node is at the chest, the shadow starts at the chest. With the feet 10 to 34 px south of a north wall the chest lies inside the 24 px footprint; in the probe the beam then renders black everywhere while the simulation reports 24,191 cells lit (P-9). With the feet closer than that the chest lies beyond the wall and the shadows are cast from the next compartment (66 % of cells wrong at s = 1). Both are the P1 lie the GDD exists to prevent: a prompt lit where the screen shows dark, or the opposite, "every time a player walks up to a wall" (Emitter Open Question 5).
62	
63	The lighting GDD (LO-10) already names the candidates (B: node at the foot, `offset` moves the texture; A: node at the chest; C: two lights; D: the simulation occludes from the chest) and the order of preference, and makes the choice a spike result (step 3b). What is missing, and what this ADR supplies, is (1) a contract precise enough to fail, (2) the lattice and frame facts that make the contract achievable and that nobody has written down, (3) the selection rule so the spike is mechanical, (4) the interface so the Avatar Presenter, Lighting and the Emitter can be built before the spike, and (5) the decision whether to keep this as its own ADR.
64	
65	### Constraints
66	- The Emitter is integer, scene-tree-free and never references a light class (TR-emitter-003). It cannot read what the renderer drew. Agreement is therefore enforced by construction (same origin, same lattice, same rectangles) and measured by test, never by feedback.
67	- One rect set serves collision, light and shadow (TR-section-011, ADR-0014). The occluder polygons are the `OCCLUDES_LIGHT` rectangles and invent no geometry (LO-11).
68	- Presentation places every node through `Placement` at an integer base-pixel position (ADR-0009 § 4, TR-pxl-005); the Avatar Presenter writes exactly `position` and `rotation` of the beam node (ADR-0019 § 7.2, TR-pc-026, TR-pc-040); Lighting writes every value member, including `offset` (LO-2, TR-light-006). The Presenter runs in stage AVATAR, Lighting in stage LIGHTING, always in that order (ADR-0009 § 3).
69	- At most `SHADOW_SLOTS_MAX` shadow-casting lights (TR-light-013): outcome C (two lights per beam) is rejected on that budget by the GDD and is not re-opened.
70	- The engine reference says nothing about these classes. Every engine claim carries a probe or UNVERIFIED.
71	- The world viewport renders at base resolution under pass A (the MVP build, ADR-0008 § 4), so light positions are sampled at base-pixel centres.
72	
73	### Requirements
74	- TR-light-015: the shadow origin matches the simulation's segment origin (foot, via `body.state` `pos_curr` / `occ_origin`) versus the chest apex, by a spike-decided mechanism (preference B, A, D; C rejected).
75	- AC-57 / AC-LO-15: for s in {1, 10, 20, 34, 44}, aim N, S, E, W and every `CHEST_POINT` row (idle, walk, run, carry, work, stagger, down), the drawn beam and the simulation agree to within 2 base px on whether the wall blocks the cone, and no row shows a beam that renders black while the simulation reports it lit. A failing row selects outcome D.
76	- The mechanism must not change the number of shadow-casting lights, must allocate nothing per frame, and must be selectable by data so that the spike result flips a constant rather than rewrites code.
77	
78	### Why the contract has to be an identity of origin, not a tolerance
79	Take a silhouette vertex V of a wall at distance d_V from an origin O. Displacing the origin by delta perpendicular to OV rotates the tangent ray through V by about delta / d_V radians. A subject at distance r beyond V is misclassified over a band of lateral width about r * delta / d_V. With the foot and the chest 45 px apart, d_V = 20 px (the AC-57 geometry) and r = 150 px that band is hundreds of pixels wide; even the 0.71 px that separates an integer node position from a cell centre gives about 5 px of band at those numbers. A criterion of the form "within 2 px at the subject" therefore cannot be met by *approximately* the same origin near a wall; it is met only when the two origins are the same point on the same lattice, and the residual is then the engine's own shadow sampling (`SHADOW_ATLAS_PX`, the filter). The probes agree with the arithmetic: moving the origin by half a cell changed the mismatch count by 3 to 10 times (P-7) and moved some mismatches beyond 2 px of the simulation's boundary (P-8).
80	
81	### The two frame facts nobody wrote down
82	1. **The lattice.** The simulation's integer coordinates name pixel cells, each a unit square *centred* on its integer coordinate (EM-20 (a); Layout LY-12 (b)). A stored rectangle `[x0, x1)` therefore has the continuous box `[x0 - 1/2, x1 - 1/2]` in simulation coordinates. In the render frame a tile or rectangle at integer origin `x0` covers `[x0, x1)`, and the occluder polygon's vertices are those integers (LO-11). So **render = simulation + 1/2** on each axis: the polygons need no shift, and the simulation's cell centre `n` is the render point `n + 1/2`. A light node written at the integer `n` (what `Placement.put` writes) sits at the *corner* of the foot's cell, 0.707 px from the cell centre the simulation uses and, when the foot cell touches a wall's east or south face, **exactly on the polygon face**, where P-6 shows whole regions flip.
83	2. **The interpolation lag.** The Presenter places the drawn foot at `Placement.at(prev, curr, alpha)`; the simulation uses `pos_curr`. They are equal at rest and when `alpha` is 1, and differ by at most one tick of travel (`V_RUN` per axis per tick, registry) otherwise. This is the same one-tick presentation lag every drawn thing has (the prompts too, LO-7), not a shadow-specific error.

116	### 2. The identity contract and its error budget
117	
118	**Definitions.** `O_sim` is the integer cell `occ_origin` of the emitter that casts the light: for a BEAM the foot (`beam_pose.occ_origin = pos_curr`), for every other emitter kind its floor-plane anchor (EM-6: "other emitter kinds use their floor-plane anchor for both"). `render(p)` is `Vector2(p) + CELL_CENTRE` with `CELL_CENTRE = (0.5, 0.5)`. `O_draw` is the global position of the shadow-casting `Light2D` node in the body frame, which P-1 shows is the point the engine casts shadows from.
119	
120	**Contract (SO-1).** For every shadow-casting light at rest (`prev == curr`, or `alpha` 1), `O_draw == render(O_sim)` exactly (a zero-error lattice identity, float32 exact up to 2^23 px, and `WORLD_COORD_LIMIT` of ADR-0015 is below that). In motion `|O_draw - render(O_sim)|` is at most one tick of travel per axis, the presentation-wide lag of §"The two frame facts" (2). The cone *apex* is separate: it is the beam's chest point and is placed by `offset` (§ 4).
121	
122	**Error budget (what is and is not a term).**
123	
124	| Term | Bound | Status |
125	|---|---|---|
126	| Lattice (integer node against cell centre) | 0 after § 3; 0.707 px (0.5 per axis) without it | removed by decision (P-7, P-8) |
127	| Interpolation lag | at most `V_RUN` per axis per tick, zero at rest | accepted, not corrected (the same lag as every drawn thing; correcting only the shadow would make the shadow lead its own beam) |
128	| Apex placement | float32 only (probe P-3: centroid error 0.00 at five angles); up to `|v| * sin(delta_theta)` (1.7 px for PC-5's 2.8 degrees) *if* `offset` is computed from a rotation other than the one on the node | removed by ordering (§ 4.3) and checked every frame by SHO-03 |
129	| Aim lead (PC-5, up to 2.8 degrees) | applies to the **cone edge**, not to the origin: probe P-1 shows the shadow origin does not depend on rotation | not an origin term; accepted by PC-5 and out of scope here |
130	| Engine shadow sampling (`SHADOW_ATLAS_PX`, `shadow_filter`) | measured by SO-P6 and SO-P8; NONE gave 8 to 16 boundary mismatches of 88,031 cells and PCF13 179 | spike-decided (§ 8) |
131	
132	**Measure (SO-2, the boundary-robust metric).** A mismatching cell counts at radius r when every cell within Chebyshev distance r has the same simulation answer; the metric is the count of mismatches *at radius r*, i.e. disagreements more than r px from any simulation boundary. "Agree to within 2 base px" (AC-57) is **zero mismatches at radius 2**; the tighter envelope that matches the project's locked +/- 1 px contracts (I-EDGE, the prompt agreement of LO-7) is **zero at radius 1**. P-8 gives the shape of the answer: with the lattice applied both are zero in all four scenes; with an integer node position radius 1 is not zero (21 cells in one scene); with a node half a cell the wrong way radius 2 is not zero (40 cells). AC-57's tolerance is therefore read as the radius-2 criterion and the radius-1 count is recorded beside it, not waived; the spike decides whether the radius-1 requirement holds under the shipped `shadow_filter` (§ 8, SO-P8).

134	### 3. The lattice: where the origin goes
135	
136	**3.1 Decision (SO-3).** Every shadow-casting `Light2D` node is positioned at `Placement.at(...)` (or the anchor, for a static emitter) **plus `CELL_CENTRE`**, written only through one new `Placement` function:
137	
138	```gdscript
139	# src/presentation/pipeline/placement.gd (ADR-0009 § 4 gains this function and this constant; Foundation ask F1)
140	## The simulation's cell n is centred on n; the render frame's pixel n spans [n, n + 1). A point-like origin on the simulation's lattice is therefore at n + CELL_CENTRE.
141	const CELL_CENTRE: Vector2 = Vector2(0.5, 0.5)
142	
143	## The only assignment point for a Light2D position. p is an integer cell (already floored by Placement.at, or an anchor). Skips an unchanged write.
144	static func put_light_origin(node: Light2D, p: Vector2i) -> void:
145		var v: Vector2 = Vector2(p) + CELL_CENTRE
146		if node.position != v:
147			node.position = v
148	```
149	
150	It applies to **every** `Light2D` Lighting or the Presenter positions, not only the six shadow-casting ones (the beam, the beacon, the lent fixtures, slot 6): one rule is cheaper to lint than a per-kind table, and it is also the more accurate origin for the non-shadow pools, whose radius test in the simulation is measured from the same cell centre (EM-22).
151	
152	**3.2 Why this and not the alternatives** (Alternatives 3 and 4). Probed: a fractional light position is honoured by the shadow (P-5) and the viewport snap flags do not round it; the half cell cuts mismatches by 3 to 10 times (P-7) and removes every beyond-radius-1 disagreement (P-8). Shifting the occluder polygons by -1/2 instead puts a polygon face through every pixel centre in pass A, which is the degenerate case, breaks LO-11's integer set equality and puts the shadow edge half a pixel off the wall art.
153	
154	**3.3 The polygon side is unchanged.** Occluder polygon vertices are the stored integer corners of the `OCCLUDES_LIGHT` rectangles in the body frame node, with no shift; the node's cull mode is `CULL_DISABLED` (P-4: `CULL_CLOCKWISE` leaks through walls for lights outside them, 35.94 % at s = 34 in P-9). The body frame offset is one floored integer per body (TR-shipbody-033), so the relation holds on every live body. Under this rule a shadow-casting light is never on a polygon face: faces are on integers and origins on half-integers, which removes the degenerate case of P-6 by parity.
155	
156	**3.4 Consequences for the placement contract (Foundation ask F1).**
157	- `PRES-03` and its named allow-list (ADR-0009 § 4, ADR-0010 § 6.6) gain exactly two entries: `Placement.put_light_origin` as the only writer of a `Light2D` `position`, and Lighting's `beam_offset_writer.gd` as the only writer of a `Light2D` `offset` (SHO-01, SHO-02).
158	- The `PLACEMENT_FRACTIONAL` post-frame sweep ("`global_position` integral within epsilon 0") exempts nodes in the group `light_origin` and asserts the *lattice* instead: the fractional part of `global_position` is exactly 0.5 on both axes (SHO-03). The sweep's own bound (integer exactness to 2^24) becomes 2^23 for these nodes, which `WORLD_COORD_LIMIT` (ADR-0015) respects with a factor of two to spare.
159	- ADR-0009 § 4's sentence "the beam's chest point and the Avatar sprite use the same rounded position" is true of the *integer cell* both start from; the light node is that cell plus `CELL_CENTRE`, the sprite is that cell. The two never disagree by more than the constant.

161	### 4. The beam: node, offset, ordering
162	
163	**4.1 Node topology and writers (fixed; this is LO-2 plus the lattice).** One `PointLight2D` per bound seat beam, a child of a **non-rotating** body-frame node (never of the avatar). The Avatar Presenter writes `position` (through `put_light_origin`) and `rotation` (raw aim for the local seat, committed aim for a remote one, ADR-0019 § 7.1); Lighting writes `offset` and every other value member. The two member sets are disjoint (TR-light-006, owned by ADR-0028; this ADR depends on it and does not restate its lint).
164	
165	**4.2 `BeamOffset`, the apex term (SO-4).** With the probed node-local, unscaled `offset` (P-2), the apex lands at `node + Rot(theta) * (offset + a)`, where `a` is the vector from the texture centre to the texture apex in the quad's local frame, in base px at the drawn scale (the sidecar's `apex_offset_texels / D_tex`, LO-15). Requiring the apex at the chest, `node + v`, gives:
166	
167	```gdscript
168	# src/presentation/lighting/beam_offset.gd  (pure; no Node; golden-vector testable headless)
169	class_name BeamOffset extends RefCounted
170	
171	## offset = Rot(-theta) * v - a. v is the integer vector from the occlusion origin to the apex (the chest offset for a beam, (0, 0) for every other light);
172	## theta is the rotation READ BACK from the node this frame; a is the texture apex displacement from the texture centre at the drawn scale.
173	static func offset_for(theta: float, vx: int, vy: int, ax: float, ay: float) -> Vector2:
174		return Vector2(float(vx), float(vy)).rotated(-theta) - Vector2(ax, ay)
175	```
176	
177	The same function serves every hard-shaped light: for a beacon or a lent fixture `v = (0, 0)` and the offset is the texture's own apex term (LO-2: "under both outcomes Lighting writes `offset` every render frame"). `OFFSET_FRAME` (LO tuning knob, "discovered") is **LOCAL** on 4.7.2 (P-2, both renderers). Only the LOCAL branch is implemented: the GDD's WORLD formula `v - Rot(theta) * a` would be dead code on every observed build; if a spike machine disagrees, the branch is added by amendment and the probe pack (SO-P2) is what reports it. Write-on-change applies (LO-3); `Vector2` is a value type, so the function allocates nothing.

Lighting reads the rotation back from the node (`light.rotation`), not from a copy, so a stale value cannot exist. The apex-equals-chest check (SHO-03) runs every frame in dev builds: it recomputes the apex from the node's actual `global_transform` and `offset` and compares it with `render(o) + v` to 0.01 px.

For a beam under B the node is at the foot and the lit region is a function of the apex. **Decided: the set is measured from the apex (the chest point), for every outcome.** Proof that nothing blocking is missed: let P be a lit point (within `reach_px` of the apex C) and F the foot; a rectangle that blocks F to P meets the segment FP at some Q, and the distance from C is convex along a segment, so `|QC| <= max(|FC|, |PC|) <= max(|v|max, reach_px)`; every beam shape's `reach_px` exceeds `|v|max` (about 45), so the rectangle is within `reach_px` of C and in the set with `OCC_MARGIN_PX` 0. 247	### Implementation Guidelines
248	
249	- **Must** position every `Light2D` through `Placement.put_light_origin` and no other path; **must never** write a shadow-casting light's `position` with `Placement.put`, `position =`, `global_position =` or any relative-move call (lint SHO-01, PRES-03).

259	## Alternatives Considered

259	## Alternatives Considered
260	
261	### Alternative 1: Fold the decision into ADR-0028
262	- **Description**: ADR-0028 (2D lighting budget and modifier chain) carries the shadow origin as one section, as the architecture note allows if the spike settles both at once.
263	- **Pros**: one fewer ADR; the Lighting-side detail lives with the rest of Lighting.
264	- **Cons**: the spike has not run, so the fold condition is false; outcome D edits the Core simulation and cannot live in a Presentation ADR; the Avatar Presenter and `emitter.place` stories need the interface before ADR-0028 is written.

266	
267	### Alternative 2: Outcome A as the default (node at the chest, accept the discrepancy)
268	- **Description**: the GDD's second preference: simplest scene, the node follows the chest point.
269	- **Pros**: no `offset` choreography beyond the texture's own apex term; no ordering dependency between AVATAR and LIGHTING.
270	- **Cons**: probed 2026-10-29 to fail exactly where AC-57 looks: a black beam while the simulation reports 24,191 cells lit (s = 20), 27 % to 66 % of cells wrong for s <= 20, and no cull mode repairs it (`CULL_CLOCKWISE` leaks 35.94 % even with the chest outside). 271	- **Rejection Reason**: kept as the control arm (§ 5), not as a candidate; shipping it would knowingly ship the P1 lie.
272	
273	### Alternative 3: Integer node position, accept the half-cell error
274	- **Description**: write the beam node with `Placement.put` (no `CELL_CENTRE`) and rely on the 2 px AC-57 tolerance.
275	- **Pros**: no new `Placement` function, no allow-list entry, no sweep exemption; the half cell is invisible to the eye.
276	- **Cons**: P-7 shows 3 to 10 times more mismatches; P-8 shows disagreements more than 1 px from the simulation's boundary (21 cells in one scene) which breaks the project's +/- 1 px contracts; a foot cell touching a wall's east or south face puts the light exactly on the polygon face, where P-6 shows whole regions flip.
277	- **Rejection Reason**: the fix is one constant and one function, and it is exact; the cost is a reviewed carve-out in ADR-0009 (Foundation ask F1), not a design cost.
278	
279	### Alternative 4: Shift the occluder polygons by -1/2 instead of the light by +1/2
280	- **Description**: keep integer light positions and move every wall polygon half a pixel up and left.
281	- **Pros**: no fractional node positions anywhere.
282	- **Cons**: puts a polygon face through every base-pixel centre under pass A (the degenerate case); breaks LO-11's integer set equality ("the union of the merged polygons equals the union of Layout's rectangles exactly"); the shadow edge no longer coincides with the wall art edge by half a pixel; every consumer of the polygons needs the shift.
283	- **Rejection Reason**: moves the error onto the one set that must be exact.
284	
285	### Alternative 5: Outcome D as the default (the simulation occludes from a chest walk-back)
286	- **Description**: change EM-6 now: the simulation's occlusion origin is the chest, walked back to the first clear point; the node follows it.
287	- **Pros**: the drawn and simulated origins coincide whatever the engine does with `offset`; no `offset` choreography for the origin.
288	- **Cons**: edits the Core Emitter contract before there is any evidence it is needed (B passes every probe); a per-tick walk query for every beam; the walk-back point jumps at wall depth; EM-6's own ruling prefers the foot ("`pos_curr` is outside every footprint by construction and free of the 2 px mirror jitter").
289	- **Rejection Reason**: it is the contingency (§ 7), specified so it is cheap, and adopted only if B and A fail.
290	
291	### Alternative 6: Two lights per beam (outcome C)
292	- **Description**: a cone at the chest plus a shadow-only caster at the foot.
293	- **Pros**: exact origin for the shadows.
294	- **Cons**: four beams become eight lights against `SHADOW_SLOTS_MAX`; breaks the shadow-slot topology (LO-9) and the lend mechanism.
295	- **Rejection Reason**: rejected by the GDD on budget; unchanged.
296	
297	### Alternative 7: A hand-built shadow (own shadow polygons drawn as dark meshes)
298	- **Description**: compute the shadow in script from the same integer rectangles and the exact origin, and draw it as geometry, bypassing the engine's shadow pass.
299	- **Pros**: exact by construction; no dependence on how the engine casts shadows.
300	- **Cons**: a second shadow system, per-frame polygon work in GDScript for up to six lights (UNVERIFIED cost, S1), no soft edge or filter, and it competes with the engine light pass it must composite against; contradicts LO-11's use of engine `LightOccluder2D`.
301	- **Rejection Reason**: unnecessary while the engine's shadow, fed the right origin, is measured to agree to within 1 px of the simulation's boundary.
302	
303	### Alternative 8: A tolerance-only contract (no origin identity)
304	- **Description**: leave the origin free and state only "agree to within 2 px" (AC-57 as written).
305	- **Pros**: no lattice rule, no ordering dependency.
306	- **Cons**: § Context's parallax arithmetic shows a tolerance on the subject cannot be met by an approximately equal origin near a wall; it makes the spike result a coin-flip.
307	- **Rejection Reason**: the identity contract is what makes the tolerance achievable; the tolerance is kept as the measure (SO-2).
308	
309	## Consequences
310	
311	### Positive
312	- The spike is mechanical: a ladder, nine probes and one table, with the answer pre-registered and the probes already shown to pass for B on one machine.
313	- The simulation does not change under B. The only presentation change is one `Placement` function, one lint allow-list entry and one sweep exemption.
314	- One lattice rule covers every light, and it removes the polygon-face degeneracy by parity.
315	- D is specified and cheap: the Presenter already takes its origin from a named source.
316	- The interface unblocks the Avatar Presenter and Lighting stories before ADR-0028 exists.
317	
318	### Negative
319	- A fractional `Light2D.position` is a deliberate exception to "every written position has a zero fractional part" (ADR-0009 § 4), which needs Foundation sign-off (F1) and a second lint rule (SHO-03 lattice check) beside the integral sweep.
320	- B has an ordering dependency (AVATAR before LIGHTING) that A would not; it is satisfied by an existing stage order, but a future change to the stage list must preserve it (SHO-03 catches a violation every frame in dev builds).
321	- B keeps a two-origin model on screen: a cone drawn from the chest with shadows cast from the feet. It is the same model the simulation uses, so they agree, but a wall footprint that lies between the chest and the foot can shade a region the chest alone would light. Whether that reads naturally is UNVERIFIED (playtest).
322	- All pre-spike evidence is from one machine and an editor build.
323	
324	## Risks
325	- **R1: the release export or the reference GPUs behave differently from the dev machine** (shadow origin from `offset`, the frame, the lattice response). *Mitigation*: the probe pack is the gate; A and D are specified; nothing is Accepted without it.
326	- **R2: the viewport snap flags round light positions on a path not probed** (the probe covered pass A with the flags on the `SubViewport`, not the root or pass B with a non-integer stretch). *Mitigation*: SO-P5 runs both passes; if snapping rounds lights, `put_light_origin` is replaced by a node-parent offset (an amendment) or the flags are turned off for the light parent.
327	- **R3: merged multi-vertex polygons and real edge-apex textures behave differently from the one-rectangle, centred-texture probes.** *Mitigation*: SO-P3 and SO-P9 use the shipping builder and textures; failure stops Acceptance.
328	- **R4: `shadow_filter` PCF widens the disagreement beyond radius 1.** *Mitigation*: SO-P8 sets the shipped level; the agreement statement is then the measured one, and a PCF level that breaks radius 2 is not shipped.
329	- **R5: the half-cell exception spreads** (other presenters copy it). *Mitigation*: `put_light_origin` takes a `Light2D`, not a `Node2D`; SHO-01 bans the pattern elsewhere.

306	### 7. The Avatar Presenter
307	
308	**7.1 Registration and reads.** `AvatarPresenter` registers a `PresenterDescriptor` at `PresentationStage.AVATAR` (2) with no `_process` (ADR-0009 § 3); its `present(frame)` reads `body.state` previous and current positions and the odometer, `ControllerView` (facing, `gait_effective`, `octant`, `loco_state`, `carry_ref`, chest and hand points, `stagger_end_tick`, `t_downed`), `emitter.state` (beam lit and shape) and `frame.alpha`, and places everything with `Placement.at` and `Placement.put` (ADR-0009 § 4: interpolate, then floor per axis, so every written position has a zero fractional part). It draws any crewmate, local or remote, from the same views with no HOST/MIRROR branch (CR-10). For the **local avatar only** it also reads the Adapter's `raw_aim()` to rotate the chest `Light2D` (the drawn cone may lead the committed cone by at most `AIM_SEND_THRESHOLD` and one send interval, the accepted divergence of PC-5); a remote avatar's beam rotates from the replicated committed `aim_angle`, which may not be coarsened below the facing hysteresis. The pre-play tokens of `AdapterViews` drive the hand's switch animation only. The Presenter keeps its `anim_counter` private.
309	
310	*Frame index.* Moving frames are `posmod(anim_counter, 8)` with `anim_counter` accumulating `dir * (cycle_pos - cycle_pos_prev)` from Body's `odometer` (D.11); the cadence test samples the Presenter once per tick through an injected `PresentFrame`, so the accumulator sees the same odometer sequence at every render rate. **The tick-stepped frames are derived from the committed tick `T`**, not from `present_time`. *Idle breathing* is free-running: `AvatarFrames.idle_frame(T)` is `posmod(floor(T / IDLE_FRAME_TICKS), 6)` with no entry tick (the GDD's `T - T_enter` needs a per-state entry tick that the block does not hold and that a catch-up frame cannot observe exactly; a breath that starts mid-cycle is invisible; GDD sync). *Work, stagger and down frames* are anchored on a sim-held entry tick through `AvatarFrames.timed_frame(T, enter_tick, ticks_per_frame, n, one_shot)`: stagger on `stagger_end_tick - STAGGER_TICKS`, down on `t_downed` (both published by the view), and the work loop on the **channel's start tick published by Interaction** (assumption on ADR-0020: the channel record carries it), so a weld animation always starts at its first frame and the GDD's work formula is unchanged. Carry-idle is the static carry frame 0 and needs no clock. Because `T` does not advance while the kernel is `PAUSED`, these freeze under pause with no special case (TR-pc-038), and because they are a pure function of committed ticks they are identical across render cadences (TR-pc-039). **This is an exception to the registry pattern `cosmetic_phase_from_tick_counter`** ("cosmetic phase uses `present_time`, never the tick counter"), which ADR-0001 and ADR-0009 own. It is a deliberate, narrow one: only `AvatarFrames`, only for the avatar's tick-stepped frames, whose per-tick output must replay byte-identically. It is a foundation ask (below) and the pattern is mechanically unlinted today (ADR-0010 § 6.6b: "No lint"), so the exception is enforced by review and by the avatar cadence test. The moving frames are driven by Body's `odometer`, a simulation value, so they need no exception; every other cosmetic (flicker, fade, the ignored-input cue) keeps `present_time`.
311	
312	**7.2 Write allow-list (TR-pc-026 is ADR-0009's; the Controller's rule list is this).** The Presenter writes exactly: the sprite `frame`, `flip_h`, the integer `position` (through `Placement.put` only), overlay `visible`, and the chest `Light2D`'s `position` and `rotation` (rotation may be fractional). It never writes `scale`, `rotation` (on the body), `skew`, `modulate`, `self_modulate` or any `Tween` or `AnimationPlayer` track on the body or its parents up to the avatar root (rule `CTL-11`, AC-PCI-207, PRES-03, PRES-04). It draws nothing beyond that and submits nothing; the Perception Filter may substitute the whole body for a horror rig but never edits pixels, moves the chest or hand point or touches the beam.
313	
314	**7.3 The sheet and sidecar checks (TR-pc-046).** "Import fails" is read as **the asset-pipeline CI gate fails the build**, not as an engine `EditorImportPlugin` (which would put an editor-only dependency in the pipeline for one check). Two checks, one library: (1) the numeric bounds, `abs(CHEST_POINT.x) <= 2` and `abs(HAND_POINT.x) <= 12` for every sheet, row and frame, are *named structural invariants* of the avatar sidecar table (`assets/data/animation/`, closed schema, ADR-0007 § 2.5) and report `PC_LINT_CHEST_POINT` and `PC_LINT_HAND_POINT` as domain-2 boot errors naming sheet, row and frame, so the same loader fails the game, the headless tests and the offline lint; (2) the lamp-plate occlusion check needs pixels, so it is a content-lint rule family `AVATAR-*` in `tools/ci/content_lint.gd` (ADR-0007 § 2.2) that loads each sheet's PNG and its per-sheet lamp-plate mask with `Image` and fails with `PC_LINT_LAMP_OCCLUDED` naming sheet, row and frame when an opaque pixel lies over the mask (AC-PCI-206). **The Presenter carries no runtime clamp** (rule `CTL-11`: `clamp(`, `clampi(` and `clampf(` are banned in `src/presentation/controller/avatar/` wherever `CHEST_POINT` or `HAND_POINT` is read), so a bad table is a build failure, never a hidden correction on screen. The lamp-plate mask and the sidecar tables do not exist yet (`/asset-spec` pending); the rule is written against a fixture mask (GDD Gaps) and the file formats are the asset-spec stage's to fix.
315	
316	**7.4 Footfalls (TR-audio-038).** Audio drives footfalls from the published `odometer` (Body's view), `gait_effective`, `octant` and `facing` (this ADR's view), never from the Presenter's `anim_counter`, which is private and has no getter. Priming the counter on restore and the one-footfall catch-up poll are ADR-0029's.

326	### 8. Body roots: canvas offset and visibility
327	
328	**Canvas offset (the formula ADR-0015 hands to this ADR).** For every body root, with `avatar_body` the avatar's current body, `off_curr(b) = world(b) - world(avatar_body)` and `off_prev(b) = world_prev(b) - world_prev(avatar_body)` using the **current** avatar body for both terms (so a body switch never interpolates across two reference frames), and `position = Placement.at(off_prev, off_curr, frame.alpha)`, written with `Placement.put` in stage 0 (`world`, `world_prev`, `vel` come from `BodyView`; `world` is exterior-only and bounded by `WORLD_COORD_LIMIT`, so every offset is within `2^23` and exact in `float32`). The avatar's body root is at (0, 0). A root whose offset did not change costs one skipped write.
329	
330	**Visibility (WM-19, defence in depth).** `BodyRoot.visible = InteriorDrawRule.visible(b, avatar_body, ...)`: true for the avatar's body and for a body docked or welded to it; false for a body drawn only as an exterior silhouette (those are not this tree). The rule is a pure function with injected inputs so it is unit-testable; its docked input is a Web Map read (an assumption on ADR-0026). Hiding a root hides its subtree and its lights' occluders are Lighting's concern.

With the transform resolved, I'm now checking where Lighting actually parents its pooled beam nodes — whether under the body root established by Placement, or somewhere else per ADR-0034's rule that BodyScenes attachment is opt-in rather than automatic.

Since the light must never be parented to the avatar directly, I need to track who reparents it on BODY_TRANSFER events like pod hops or welds; otherwise the foot-coordinate light could sit in the wrong frame for a frame, causing a shadow-origin glitch. This looks like a real gap: nothing currently owns the beam light's parent assignment or its reparenting rule during BODY_TRANSFER, though the Y-sort concern for Light2D nodes turns out to be harmless since lights aren't drawn as sorted items.

I also want to check whether Godot 4's canvas light culling against the light quad in the viewport renderer matches what I recall about occluder handling — I'm recalling the renderer's shadow rect computation logic.

Setting up shadow light transforms...

Now for lights that cast shadows, I need to gather occluders per canvas, transforming each occluder's shape by its canvas transform and checking whether it intersects the combined shadow bounding rect, building a linked list of qualifying occluders to later render into each light's shadowmap.

I'm confirming the rect_cache calculation includes texture_offset, and that the shadow far distance (radius_cache * 1.1) is based on the diagonal of the occluder quad measured from the light's origin — so culling happens against the union of all shadow-casting quads currently in view, across up to six shadow-casting lights.

I'm now checking whether this far-plane margin is actually sufficient for an edge-apex cone shape, where the apex sits at one edge of the texture rather than centered. If the cone has reach R and width W, the quad dimensions become roughly R × W with diagonal sqrt(R²+W²), but the farthest corner distance from the foot point could actually exceed 1.1 times that diagonal depending on how W compares to R — meaning the margin might not always be safe.

I realize this culling behavior comes from Godot's quad-based culling including texture offset, with far plane set at 1.1× the quad diagonal from the node—but since all my probes used 1200×1200 textures in a 400×300 viewport, the quad always covered the whole scene, masking this effect entirely. This is a real finding: I should mitigate it by padding the texture quad so it reliably contains both the foot and its reach, accepting some fill-rate cost on the mostly-transparent extra area, or add a "padded quad" variant to my test ladder.

I should also flag that OCC_MARGIN_PX in §4.4 governs lighting-side culling, which is separate from engine-side quad culling—meaning OQ-E likely underestimates the actual margin needed, and this needs confirmation via probe rather than relying on my memory of the engine source.

I also want to double check ADR-0009's placement logic—whether it defines Placement.at and the PLACEMENT_FRACTIONAL sweep, with stage numbers AVATAR=2 and LIGHTING=6—so I'll do a quick grep to verify.

I'm noticing TR-pc-026's "floored lerp" description conflicts with ADR-0018's fractional 0.5 value, which is already flagged under F1, but the TR text itself still needs a sync check against the GDD sync list that includes LO-10, LO-2, and OFFSET_FRAC items.

I'm also finding the sync list omits two important rows — the player-controller rule behind TR-pc-026 and PR-4 rule 2 (TR-pxl-005, requiring every node including the beam chest point to be floored to integer base px). This is a real gap: the Foundation exception in ADR-0018 contradicts both GDD TR rows without acknowledgment, which I'd flag as medium-severity and blocking since it's an Accepted ADR conflicting with GDD requirements.

Separately, I'm checking staleness in ADR-0018's "Last Verified" notes — it claims ADR-0017 isn't yet on disk, but it actually is, and ADR-0017's content around the `origin`/occlusion_origin field and the D5.3 section needs reconciling against ADR-0018 §7's requirement for a published prev/curr pair.

Grepping ADR-0017 for "occ_origin" turns up nothing — it only computes occlusion_origin as a function from BodyView rather than publishing it as a persisted field, while ADR-0018 depends on beam_pose.occ_origin existing as a field. That's fine under option B where the presenter reads body.state directly, but matters more for option D where the published pair is required. I'm also confirming the chest point handling: ADR-0017 has the presenter reading ControllerView.chest_point, and ADR-0018's chest offset calculation (v = chest_sim - foot, using committed-tick position) checks out as consistent, including the mirrored offset and the abs(x)≤2 constraint on CHEST_POINT.

Then I'm checking the apex comparison for SHO-03, which matches render(o) + v within tolerance, and confirming rotation semantics stay consistent for local seat handling.

I'm now flagging an inconsistency in §6: the boot invariant LIGHT_SHADOW_ORIGIN_COMBO reads an Emitter tuning value OCC_ORIGIN_MODE that doesn't actually exist in ADR-0017, and the mode-switch/reserved-D design looks like speculative generality — the claim that a spike result "just flips a constant" doesn't hold since mode D actually requires new code, and the CHEST_NODE control arm (A) ends up shipping as unused code for a solo MVP, which is a right-sizing concern worth raising.

The verification plan is heavy: a ScalarTable row, boot combo invariant, 6 lint rules, 9 probes, and a 140-row matrix per configuration across roughly 16 configs implies thousands of retained screenshots, which conflicts with AC-57's expectation of ~20 named evidence screenshots per config — I'd recommend running the full matrix only on the pinned config (Forward+ Vulkan, release, both RMs) and a reduced subset elsewhere, flagged as low severity and non-blocking. I'm also noting overlap in the lint pack — SHO-06's vertex check duplicates LO-11/ADR-0028 tests, and SHO-05 duplicates the token+boot check — plus a question about whether the spike-gating claim that existing probes already support option B still holds once the full-circle 1200px case is considered.

Checking the SO-P7 140-row math confirms it's just aim directions times s times 7 rows, so that's fine. I'm also verifying that the occluder-distance proof in §4.4 correctly covers edge cases like foot-at-wall footprints, that rotation-writing responsibility for non-beam hard-shaped lights falls to Lighting itself, and that the body-frame parenting requirement in ADR-0034/ADR-0018 means the parent node must be the actor's body root since it changes with movement.

Now I'm tracing through a BODY_TRANSFER scenario like a pod hop or weld/detach frame shift: who reparents the beam light? ADR-0034 only reparents the Presenter node, which leaves a gap -- if the light stays under the old root during a pod hop, there's an origin error equal to the body offset until reparenting happens. For weld rebasing, the timing seems to work out fine as long as the parent root is correct, but I think ADR-0018 needs to explicitly state the parenting rule (beam light parented to the actor's BodyRoot, reparented via BodyScenes on BODY_TRANSFER) or clearly delegate that responsibility to ADR-0028/0034, so I'll flag this as a finding with cross-ADR ownership.

I'm resolving this as: state the rule in ADR-0018 §4.1, with ADR-0034 as the implementing owner -- attach the beam Light2D through BodyScenes so the existing BODY_TRANSFER reparent logic covers it automatically. I also confirm SHO-04's translation-only BodyRoot assumption holds, that y-sorting doesn't matter for non-drawn Light2D nodes, that Lighting creating pooled Light2D nodes outside BodyScenes is permitted per ADR-0034, and that occluders from other welded/docked bodies sitting under different roots are fine since their offsets are integral. Now I'm turning to consider Pass B.

Everything else checks out -- engine version stamped, post-cutoff API risks honestly flagged, GDD linked, alternatives genuine, consequences mostly honest, decision maker noted as Claude acting autonomously. But I catch a stale note saying ADR-0017 and ADR-0028 aren't on disk yet, when ADR-0017 actually is now, so that needs reconciling. More importantly, there's a real cross-ADR mismatch: ADR-0017's beam_pose has no `occ_origin` field or OCC_ORIGIN_MODE, and only tracks occlusion_origin changing via D, while ADR-0018 §7 wants a prev/curr pair published in beam_pose rather than just the function output. I need to decide ownership -- should ADR-0017 reserve the OCC_ORIGIN_MODE field, or should ADR-0018 drop its dependency on an Emitter-side mode row since only FOOT currently exists, making the boot invariant unnecessary? I'm leaning toward right-sizing by dropping the complexity for now.

I think the cleanest fix is to cut the cross-module boot combo invariant entirely until D is actually adopted, since with Emitter hard-coded to foot and Lighting's SHADOW_ORIGIN_MODE only having two legal values that both resolve to FOOT, the combo check currently verifies nothing at ship time. So I'll recommend removing the OCC_ORIGIN_MODE reservation and LIGHT_SHADOW_ORIGIN_COMBO check now, and have D's future amendment reintroduce them -- that resolves the mismatch with less moving machinery, owned by ADR-0018.

For ADR-0017, I also want to flag that its R8 claim of "change confined to occlusion_origin" doesn't quite hold under D's requirement for a prev/curr occ_origin pair, since deriving the previous value would need chest's previous position too, which isn't stored. I'll mark this as a minor, non-blocking cross-ADR item for ADR-0017 to amend R8/D5.3, alongside noting TR-pc-026/TR-pxl-005 sync and a potential conflict with ADR-0019's zero-fractional-part invariant.

Now I'm checking ADR-0009's F1/F2 Foundation ask around PLACEMENT_FRACTIONAL sweeping every Node2D -- this is a real blocker, since ADR-0018 can't be Accepted until ADR-0009 resolves F1, with Alternative 3 as fallback. For engine culling, I'm weighing whether to actually verify with a probe, but headless Godot can't render and a windowed run is too heavy for this review, so I'll state the finding as source-derived and require a dedicated probe (SO-P10) instead, flagging it HIGH severity and blocking since the probe pack needs to cover the padded-quad B-variant case or risk the spike passing on invalid evidence.

I also want to confirm the GDD's LO-15 cone textures use an edge-apex layout, which they do. Before finalizing, I'm thinking I should briefly consult the advisor, so I'll compose my findings and reach out before submitting the final review.

Though the advisor warns against adding a culling finding, I think there's a real flaw here: the ADR's OQ-E framing around OCC_MARGIN_PX misses that engine culling against the offset quad would break wholly-contained walls, and since every probe used a full-viewport 1200x1200 texture, none of them could have actually tested this case — so B passing P-9 with zero mismatches doesn't actually validate B here.

I'll note this as a non-blocking medium finding about an evidence gap rather than a direct contradiction, since the real issue is that a padded-texture fix could preserve B instead of jumping to the heavier D option. Before writing it up, I want to run the two greps and do a quick reconciliation pass to confirm.

I'm checking the registry rules around presentation coordinates and node transforms — confirming that Vector2i/Vector2 conversions and position/transform writes are only supposed to happen through Placement.put or put_control, which means put_light_origin looks like it's violating that constraint.

Checking beam_offset_writer.gd, since Light2D is a Node2D, its offset writes also appear to violate the allow-list, so I'm flagging that the registry needs about three amendments. input.verdict: CONCERNS. The decision itself is sound and the spike gating is stated honestly. The problem statement is clear, with the parallax arithmetic and the two frame facts. The eight alternatives were genuinely weighed. The negative consequences are stated, including the two-origin model, the fractional-position exception and the single-machine evidence. The engine is stamped as Godot 4.7.2, and the domain is marked HIGH risk with every engine claim probed or UNVERIFIED. TR-light-015 is decided here, and the owned-elsewhere rows are mapped. Three things must be amended before Accept, but none needs a rewrite. First, the lattice exception contradicts three registry stances and two live TR rows, and nothing syncs them. Second, the boot combination invariant in section 6 depends on an Emitter tuning row that the now-written ADR-0017 does not have, and the check is vacuous at ship. Third, no one owns the beam Light2D's parent across BODY_TRANSFER, and the identity contract fails on a pod hop or a weld rebase. The non-blocking items cover sibling wording, an evidence gap in the probes that support rung B, and right-sizing.

findings.text: The CELL_CENTRE lattice rule (§ 3.1) and the offset writer (§ 4.2) contradict binding registry stances and live TR rows, and the ADR syncs neither. docs/registry/architecture.yaml line 961 says presentation coordinates are integer-valued float32, converted from Vector2i only at Placement.put and the canvas_transform write; put_light_origin adds a third conversion site that writes a non-integer value. Line 971 (sim_motion_interpolation) says positions are written only through Placement.put or put_control. Line 1398, the forbidden pattern, says the position, global position, offset and transform of any Node2D are written only in placement.gd and the named allow-list. Light2D is a Node2D, so beam_offset_writer.gd breaks this rule directly; F2's note 'distinct from Sprite2D.offset' does not exempt it. TR-pxl-005 (every node at integer base px, 'incl. the beam chest point', PR-4 rule 2) and TR-pc-026 (Light2D position by a 'floored lerp with zero fractional part') are contradicted too. Yet the 'GDD syncs this ADR requests' list in § Related names only the lighting and emitter GDDs. An Accepted ADR would then contradict three registry rows and two TR rows.
findings.amendment: Extend F1 and F2 to name registry rows 961, 971 and 1398 and request their amendment together with the ADR-0009 § 4 and ADR-0010 § 6.6 changes. Row 961 gains put_light_origin as a conversion site for Light2D lattice positions. Row 971 notes that a Light2D position is Placement.at plus CELL_CENTRE through put_light_origin. Row 1398's allow-list gains placement.gd put_light_origin (Light2D position) and lighting/beam_offset_writer.gd (Light2D offset). Add two entries to § Related's GDD sync list: pixel-perfect-render-pipeline-camera.md PR-4 rule 2, and the player-controller-input.md rule behind TR-pc-026. Both should read 'Light2D position is the floored cell plus CELL_CENTRE'. Re-word the TR-pxl-005 and TR-pc-026 rows to match. Make Acceptance of ADR-0018 conditional on ADR-0009 accepting F1 (OQ-A), as Validation already implies.

findings.text: Section 6's boot invariant LIGHT_SHADOW_ORIGIN_COMBO checks the pair (Emitter OCC_ORIGIN_MODE, SHADOW_ORIGIN_MODE). It assumes 'OCC_ORIGIN_MODE is reserved in ADR-0017's tuning with one value (FOOT)'. ADR-0017 is now on disk and has no OCC_ORIGIN_MODE row and no occ_origin field. Its D5.3 implements the foot origin as the function EmitterDerived.occlusion_origin, and D5.3/R8 say the spike changes that function 'and nothing else'. At ship the only reachable pairs are (FOOT, 0) and (FOOT, 1), both legal, so the invariant can never fire. It still costs a cross-module data row, a domain-2 boot code reserved through F3, test SHO-T5 and the 2x3 matrix. Separately, the Last Verified line still says ADR-0017 is not yet on disk.
findings.amendment: Remove the Emitter-side OCC_ORIGIN_MODE reservation, the LIGHT_SHADOW_ORIGIN_COMBO invariant, its F3 boot-code reservation and SHO-T5 from the present decision. SHADOW_ORIGIN_MODE keeps values {0 FOOT_OFFSET, 1 CHEST_NODE}. State in § 7 that the outcome-D amendment adds value 2, the Emitter mode row and the combination invariant together, so the check exists only when it can fail. Re-verify every ADR-0017 statement in Cross-ADR Assumptions and Last Verified against the ADR-0017 text now on disk, for example 'occ_origin' as computed by occlusion_origin(row, out_xy) and not a stored beam_pose field. The registry beam_pose expression (entities.yaml 4274, occ_origin = pos_curr) already backs the semantics.

findings.text: Section 4.1 makes the beam PointLight2D 'a child of a non-rotating body-frame node (never of the avatar)'. The Presenter writes its position as the actor's foot in the frame of body_of_actor. Nothing says which node that parent is, or who reparents the light when the actor's body changes. ADR-0034 § 8 reparents only the Presenter node on BODY_TRANSFER, in stage 0. ADR-0034's assumptions leave Lighting's pooled nodes outside BodyScenes 'unless it chooses to'. On a pod hop, or when the parent root is wrong for any frame, the light is placed in the wrong frame and O_draw differs from render(O_sim) by the inter-body canvas offset. That is the P1 drawn-against-simulated lie that SO-1 exists to prevent. SHO-03 checks only the fractional lattice, so it cannot catch a wrong-root error. findings.text: The evidence cited for rung B ('the 2026-10-29 probes already support B', P-9 '0 mismatches at every s') does not exercise a light quad that excludes the foot. The 'Not probed' list names both 'a textured cone with the real edge-apex layout' and 'occluder culling by the light's range'. Under B with an edge-apex cone (LO-15), the quad starts at the chest and points along the aim. A wall lying wholly between the foot and the apex, for example AC-57 s = 1 aiming north, can sit outside the quad.
